chunks: About a man who has fluid in his eyes, and the fluid is removed from them, so he lies on his back for many days, forty days or less or more, and he is prevented from performing the salat except by gesture while he remains in that condition.
So he said: “There is no harm in that.”

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: by gesture or indication in place of full bodily movement
key_terms.سَمَاعَةُ: Samā‘ah, the narrator asking the Imam
key_terms.فَيَسْتَلْقِي: he lies flat on his back
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat by gestures while lying on one's back due to illness or eye treatment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a sick person whose medical condition prevents normal performance of salat. It indicates that if one can only pray by gesture while lying on his back during treatment and recovery, that is permissible and carries no blame.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: about a man who has an eye condition (cataracts or similar) and undergoes a procedure to remove the issue, requiring him to lie on his back for many days—forty days, or possibly fewer or more. As a result, he can only perform his prayers by gestures due to his condition.
The response was: "There is no harm in that."
